title: Handwriting and Fine Motor Changes in Parkinson's
content: Parkinson's disease can affect fine motor control and repetitive hand movements. Some people may notice that handwriting becomes smaller, tighter or more difficult to produce, a change often called micrographia. Fine motor tasks such as buttoning clothes, using utensils, typing or handling small objects may also become slower or more difficult. These changes can be related to bradykinesia, rigidity or tremor. Handwriting or fine motor difficulty alone does not establish Parkinson's disease because many other conditions can cause similar problems. Persistent or worsening changes should be discussed with an appropriate healthcare professional.
